title: A Novel Prompt Tuning for Graph Transformers: Tailoring Prompts to Graph Topologies

problem.claim: Uniform prompts in DeepGPT cannot dynamically tailor feature transformation to input graphs with different topological structures.

gap.claim: Existing lightweight graph prompt tuning does not account for topology-dependent feature interactions between nodes.

contributions.claim: TGPT provides topo-specific prompts tailored to the topological structures of input graphs.
TGPT learns graphlet and frequency embeddings to generate prompts from graphlet statistics.
TGPT uses node-level, graph-level, and task-specific prompts inserted into graph nodes for topology-specific feature transformation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method outperforms existing lightweight fine-tuning methods and DeepGPT in molecular graph classification and regression with comparable parameters.

narrative_sequence.summary: DeepGPT tunes continuous prompts and reduces training storage usage.
DeepGPT's uniform prompts are limited for graphs with varied structures because feature interactions depend on topology.
TGPT generates topology-specific prompts using graphlet and frequency embeddings derived from graphlet statistics.
Node-level, graph-level, and task-specific prompts are inserted into graph nodes to perform topology-specific feature transformation.
The authors report improved performance over lightweight fine-tuning methods and DeepGPT on molecular graph classification and regression with comparable parameters.

source_observation.claim: Graph structures determine different feature interactions between nodes, while uniform prompts do not dynamically adapt to graph topology.

interpretation.claim: Parameter-efficient adaptation may benefit from conditioning prompts on structural statistics rather than using one shared prompt.

application.claim: For graph models, consider generating node-, graph-, or task-level prompts from topology-derived representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether topology-specific prompting helps outside the reported molecular graph classification and regression tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical performance differences.
The abstract does not report training or inference costs beyond comparable parameter counts.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or details of the graphlet and frequency representations.
